method: All 30 initially NOT_REVIEWED canonical records now have selective online source-SCOPE checks (27 direct page comparisons, 3 USCCB search-index excerpts because direct fetch returned HTTP 403). All 30 remain NOT_REVIEWED for full English/French/Latin text line-by-line historical edition collation and for independent original printed-book facsimile certification. Original language corpus texts, 18 previous anchor reviews, 16 original novenas, and Lab Ora Rosary unchanged. Some donor adaptation labels (VERBATIM or TYPOGRAPHY_NORMALIZED) are explicitly qualified by source-scope notices where materially inaccurate.

rows.title: Morning Offering
rows.sourceAnchor: for the intentions of the Holy Father this month
rows.appAnchor: for the intentions of the Holy Father. Amen.
rows.sourceScope: USCCB published Morning Offering supplies comparable English text but contains an extra 'this month' qualifier after Holy Father's intentions. App omits it; the existing prayer is not a verbatim copy of that cited USCCB page.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited USCCB Morning Offering includes “this month” after the Holy Father's intentions. This inherited prayer omits that phrase. The two English wordings are not identical; the original French and Latin versions remain independently uncollated.
readerDisclosure.fr: La prière du matin publiée par l’USCCB ajoute « this month » après les intentions du Saint-Père. Le texte anglais conservé dans l’application omet ces mots. Les versions française et latine n’ont pas fait l’objet d’une collation indépendante.

rows.title: My Lord and My God
rows.sourceScope: John 20:28 (Thomas's confession) is directly present in the cited USCCB chapter. The standalone app acclamation is a devotional use of that single verse, not an edition-specific three-language prayer-book transcription. USCCB English does not authenticate independent historic Latin/French prayer texts.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited John 20:28 contains Thomas’s acclamation. Its use here as a short prayer is devotional; this modern English Bible page is not a certificate of the app’s historical French or Latin wording.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le lien vers Jn 20,28 donne l’acclamation de Thomas. Son emploi ici comme courte prière est dévotionnel ; cette page biblique anglaise moderne ne certifie pas les versions historiques française ou latine.

rows.title: Confiteor
rows.sourceScope: The 1962 Latin online transcription separates the minister's et vobis fratres from the faithful/minister reply et tibi pater. The app uses et tibi pater and is not the priest's et vobis fratres version. The linked original-print 1962 Missal facsimile is not independently collated; online Latin is secondary transcription.

readerDisclosure.en: This Confiteor has “et tibi, pater” (“to you, Father”), the minister/faithful form at the altar, not the priest’s “et vobis, fratres”. The linked 1962 online text is a secondary transcription; the original Missal edition is not independently collated.
readerDisclosure.fr: Ce Confiteor emploie « et tibi, pater » (« à vous, mon Père »), forme du ministre ou des fidèles, et non « et vobis, fratres » du célébrant. La transcription en ligne de 1962 est secondaire ; le Missel imprimé n’a pas été collationné indépendamment.

rows.title: Consecration to Immaculate Heart
rows.sourceScope: Fatima Center posts the full English consecration and its structure, but begins 'Oh' (app 'O') and later says 'Assist us in imitating You' (app 'Thee'); legacy VERBATIM label is too strong for this digital witness. No FR/LA source bodies present and other Pius XII or Fatima acts must not be substituted.

readerDisclosure.en: The Fatima Center publishes this English consecration, but its opening uses “Oh” where the app uses “O”, and it later says “You” rather than “Thee”. This is a close English variant, not a certified verbatim copy. No French or Latin original is claimed.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le Fatima Center publie cette consécration anglaise, mais écrit « Oh » au début (contre « O » dans l’application) et « You » plus loin (contre « Thee »). C’est une variante anglaise proche, non une copie certifiée mot à mot. Aucun original français ou latin n’est revendiqué.

rows.title: Spiritual Communion
rows.sourceAnchor: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Blessed Sacrament
rows.appAnchor: My Jesus, I believe that You are present
rows.sourceScope: Vatican News posts two distinct Spiritual Communion prayers: the first attributed to St Alphonsus Liguori follows the app's English with case/lineation differences; the second by Cardinal Merry del Val is deliberately not part of the same canonical prayer. This English online witness does not independently certify app Latin/French texts.

readerDisclosure.en: This card uses the first Spiritual Communion prayer on Vatican News, attributed there to Saint Alphonsus Liguori. The subsequent prayer by Cardinal Merry del Val is a separate text, not an omitted stanza. French and Latin editions have not been independently certified.
readerDisclosure.fr: Cette carte utilise la première communion spirituelle publiée par Vatican News, attribuée à saint Alphonse de Liguori. La prière suivante du cardinal Merry del Val est distincte, non une strophe omise. Les versions française et latine restent sans certification indépendante.

rows.title: O Salutaris Hostia
rows.sourceScope: The historical With God Benediction page gives 'O saving Victim, opening wide / The gate of heav'n to man below'; the app's English paraphrases 'open wide the gate of heaven to us below'. The witness supports hymn identity but not the literal edited English text or full French/Latin translation.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited historical hymn gives “O saving Victim, opening wide”; the app reads “O saving Victim, open wide”. The English stanza is a traditional adaptation, not a verbatim reproduction of that edition.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le cantique historique cité porte « O saving Victim, opening wide », tandis que l’application donne « O saving Victim, open wide ». La strophe anglaise est adaptée et non reproduite mot à mot de cette édition.

rows.title: Tantum Ergo
rows.sourceScope: The With God Benediction book prints the traditional English Down in adoration falling and distinguishes the historical hymn. The app is rewrapped/modernized with punctuation and line grouping. The source provides an English comparator, not a fully matched FR/LA print witness.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited historical book prints the English “Down in adoration falling” hymn. The app preserves its opening but modernizes punctuation and line grouping; this does not certify exact historical typography or the French and Latin versions.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le recueil historique cité donne l’hymne anglais « Down in adoration falling ». L’application en conserve l’incipit mais adapte la ponctuation et les vers ; ni la typographie exacte ni les versions française et latine ne sont certifiées.

rows.title: Divine Praises
rows.sourceScope: USCCB indexed English page reproduces 14 Divine Praises and cites Holy Communion and Worship of the Eucharistic Mystery outside Mass no. 99. App English invocation list agrees in scope but differs in capitalization. The USCCB page returned 403 in direct reader; comparison is from search-indexed excerpt, not direct fetch or full Latin/French collation.

readerDisclosure.en: The indexed USCCB Divine Praises page gives the current 14-invocation English form (ritual no. 99). The app retains traditional capitalization. The page was accessible through indexed excerpts, not direct retrieval; this does not certify the app’s French or Latin recensions.
readerDisclosure.fr: Les extraits indexés de l’USCCB donnent les 14 louanges de la forme anglaise actuelle (rituel, no 99). L’application conserve une capitalisation traditionnelle. La page n’a été consultable que par extrait indexé, non directement ; les textes français et latin ne sont pas certifiés.

rows.title: Litany of the Most Blessed Sacrament
rows.sourceAnchor: Living Bread, that camest down from heaven
rows.appAnchor: Living Bread which came down from heaven
rows.sourceScope: 1911 With God/Litanies Litany of the Blessed Sacrament has more invocations than current app: e.g. Supersubstantial bread, Medicine of immortality and other petitions omitted; app paraphrases several titles and closes with selected versicles/collect. Legacy TYPOGRAPHY_NORMALIZED understates abridgement. Historical 300-day indulgence references on the book must not be treated as current grants.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited historical Litany has additional invocations absent from this card, including “Supersubstantial bread” and “Medicine of immortality”. This is an abridged, reworded devotional selection—not merely normalized typography or a full verbatim transcription. Historical indulgence notes are not current grants.
readerDisclosure.fr: Les Litanies historiques citées contiennent des invocations absentes de cette carte, notamment « Supersubstantial bread » et « Medicine of immortality ». C’est un choix dévotionnel abrégé et reformulé, non une simple normalisation typographique ni une transcription intégrale. Les indulgences anciennes ne valent pas concession actuelle.

rows.title: Versicle & Prayer (English)
rows.sourceAnchor: Replenished with all sweetness and delight
rows.sourceScope: With God prints V Thou hast given them bread from heaven / R Replenished with all sweetness and delight. App has You have given them Bread from Heaven / Having within it all sweetness, a valid but different English translation. Collect likewise contemporary syntax; no exact print-English or original FR/Latin collation.

readerDisclosure.en: The historical Benediction book prints “Replenished with all sweetness and delight”; this card says “Having within it all sweetness”. The response and collect use different English wording, not a verbatim transcription of that edition.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le recueil historique de bénédiction donne « Replenished with all sweetness and delight », tandis que cette carte porte « Having within it all sweetness ». Le répons et l’oraison utilisent une autre traduction anglaise, non la transcription littérale de cette édition.

rows.title: Lord, I Am Not Worthy
rows.sourceScope: 1962 online Latin Ordinary prints Domine non sum dignus for the priest and again for the response associated with Communion of the faithful (each ter). The standalone canonical Prayer Library card is the formula, not an instruction to attribute priest's repetitions or liturgical role to the lay reader. Secondary online transcription only.

readerDisclosure.en: The 1962 Mass text prints “Domine, non sum dignus” both in the priest’s Communion and before Communion of the faithful. This card gives the prayer, not the priest’s ritual action or repetitions; the complete printed Missal remains uncollated.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le texte de la messe de 1962 donne « Domine, non sum dignus » pour la communion du prêtre et avant celle des fidèles. Cette carte présente la prière, sans attribuer au lecteur les gestes ou répétitions du célébrant ; le Missel imprimé reste à collationner.

rows.title: Leonine Prayers After Low Mass
rows.sourceAnchor: The Priest with the people recites the Mail Mary thrice
rows.sourceScope: Historic pocket prayer-book prints three Ave Marias, Salve Regina, collect, St Michael invocation and Sacred Heart three times. App preserves the sequence, but wording differs: historic St Michael 'malice and snares' and 'by thy divine power thrust' versus app 'wickedness and snares' and 'by the power of God, cast'. Historic indulgence grants on book not current.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited book confirms the historic Leonine order after Low Mass, but its Saint Michael prayer says “malice” and “thrust”, while this card says “wickedness” and “cast”. The prayers are a traditional English composite, not a verbatim copy of this edition; old indulgence statements are historical only.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le livre atteste l’ordre historique des prières léonines après la messe basse, mais sa prière à saint Michel dit « malice » et « thrust », contre « wickedness » et « cast » dans cette carte. Il s’agit d’un ensemble anglais traditionnel, non d’une copie mot à mot ; les indulgences anciennes n’ont qu’une portée historique.

rows.title: Come, Holy Spirit
rows.sourceAnchor: who have taught the hearts of the faithful
rows.appAnchor: who by the light of the Holy Spirit did instruct
rows.sourceScope: USCCB indexed Prayer to the Holy Spirit has opening Come Holy Spirit and collect 'O God, who have taught the hearts of the faithful' whereas app keeps the older 'who by the light of the Holy Spirit did instruct'. Direct USCCB page fetch returned 403: indexed excerpt only. French/Latin and exact old collect edition remain uncertified.

readerDisclosure.en: The indexed USCCB prayer uses “who have taught the hearts of the faithful”; the app keeps the older English “who ... did instruct”. The linked page was compared through indexed excerpts because direct retrieval was blocked. French and Latin are not independently collated.
readerDisclosure.fr: La prière indexée de l’USCCB emploie « who have taught the hearts of the faithful » ; l’application conserve l’ancienne traduction « who ... did instruct ». La page n’a été comparée que par extrait indexé, son accès direct étant bloqué. Le français et le latin ne sont pas collationnés indépendamment.

rows.title: Prayer to St. Michael
rows.sourceScope: The 29 September 2018 Holy See communiqué prints the Latin Saint Michael prayer and an English rendering using 'cast into hell'; the inherited English uses 'thrust into hell'. Source supports prayer identity, not identical English wording or the French translation.

readerDisclosure.en: The Holy See communiqué prints the Latin prayer and an English version using “cast into hell”; this inherited translation says “thrust into hell”. The French version was not independently collated.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le communiqué du Saint-Siège publie le latin et une traduction anglaise avec « cast into hell » ; la version conservée emploie « thrust into hell ». La traduction française reste à collationner indépendamment.

rows.title: Memorare to St. Joseph
rows.sourceScope: Diocese of Sacramento posts a Memorare to St Joseph whose English says 'my great protector, Saint Joseph' and 'spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary', whereas app says 'my sweet protector St. Joseph' and 'spouse of the Virgin Mary'. This is an established traditional variant, not exact English witness; FR/LA not witnessed.

readerDisclosure.en: The Diocese of Sacramento’s English Memorare says “my great protector”, while this card says “my sweet protector”. It also names the Blessed Virgin Mary more fully. The link confirms the prayer family, not a verbatim English text or its French and Latin versions.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le Souvenez-vous de saint Joseph publié par le diocèse de Sacramento dit « my great protector », tandis que cette carte donne « my sweet protector ». Le lien confirme la famille de prière, non une copie anglaise mot à mot ni les versions française et latine.

rows.title: Consecration to Christ the King
rows.sourceAnchor: Dómine Iesu Christe, te confíteor Regem universálem
rows.appAnchor: O Jesus Christ, I acknowledge Thee as universal King
rows.sourceScope: ITheca under Oratio ad Iesum Christum Regem publishes the full accented Latin prayer. ICKSP publishes a Latin and independent English rendering which begins 'O Lord Jesus Christ, I acknowledge Thee King of the Universe', distinct from the app's 'O Jesus Christ ... universal King'. The original iTheca link itself does not certify app English/French; historical 1923 attribution is separate.

readerDisclosure.en: ITheca provides the traditional Latin act to Christ the King. The Institute of Christ the King separately prints an English form beginning “O Lord Jesus Christ”, rather than this card’s “O Jesus Christ”. These are related witnesses, not a certified identical three-language 1923 edition.
readerDisclosure.fr: ITheca fournit l’acte latin traditionnel au Christ-Roi. L’Institut du Christ-Roi publie une version anglaise commençant par « O Lord Jesus Christ », différente du « O Jesus Christ » de cette carte. Ce sont des témoins apparentés, non une même édition trilingue certifiée.

supportingWitness.en: Institute of Christ the King · English and Latin comparator
supportingWitness.fr: Institut du Christ-Roi · témoin anglais et latin

rows.title: Prayer for the Pope
rows.sourceAnchor: V. Let us pray for Leo XIV, our Pope.
rows.appAnchor: ℣. Let us pray for our Sovereign Pontiff N.
rows.sourceScope: Vatican News's currently published Prayer for the Pope is an abbreviated current-language arrangement naming the pope, followed by a collect; the inherited app has a placeholder N., adds Tu es Petrus, and retains a longer historical form. The source is comparative, not an exact complete-text citation.

readerDisclosure.en: The linked Vatican News prayer is a current arrangement naming the Pope and giving a shorter collect. This historical composite also includes “Thou art Peter” and retains N. as a placeholder. The linked page is a comparison, not its full original edition.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le texte de Vatican News nomme le pape et donne une oraison plus courte. Cette forme historique composite comprend aussi « Tu es Pierre » et conserve N. comme emplacement à compléter. Le lien sert de comparaison, non de preuve d’identité textuelle intégrale.

rows.title: Si quæris miracula — St Anthony for Lost Things
rows.sourceScope: Preces Latinae publishes Latin and English Si quaeris with an abbreviated repeated antiphon 'Ant: Cedunt mare, vincula...' while app writes out its English/Latin refrain at each repetition and includes the collect; this is a performance expansion, not strictly verbatim source typography. Source notes Julian of Speyer association and rejects unsupported Bonaventure author attribution.

readerDisclosure.en: The bilingual responsory witness abbreviates repeated antiphons with an ellipsis; this card expands those repeated lines for prayer. The source also distinguishes a possible Julian of Speyer origin from an unproven attribution to Saint Bonaventure. The expansion is not an exact photographic transcription.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le témoin bilingue abrège les antiennes reprises avec des points de suspension ; cette carte développe les reprises pour la prière. La source distingue l’attribution possible à Julien de Spire de celle, non établie, à saint Bonaventure. La reprise développée n’est pas une transcription photographique exacte.

rows.title: Act of Reparation to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
rows.sourceAnchor: Iesu dulcissime, cuius effusa in homines caritas
rows.appAnchor: Most Sweet Jesus, whose overflowing charity
rows.sourceScope: Apostolic Penitentiary 2002 Enchiridion page gives the Latin Actus reparationis Iesu dulcissime and distinct indulgence provision. It does not print a matched official English or French translation, so donor language-quality claims cannot be independent certified equivalence. Source text remains unchanged and no new indulgence grant is asserted.

readerDisclosure.en: The Apostolic Penitentiary’s Enchiridion prints the Latin Act of Reparation “Iesu dulcissime” and its indulgence provision. This Latin source does not certify the exact English translation beginning “Most Sweet Jesus” or the French version.
readerDisclosure.fr: L’Enchiridion de la Pénitencerie apostolique imprime en latin l’acte de réparation « Iesu dulcissime » et la concession associée. Ce témoin latin ne certifie pas à lui seul la traduction anglaise « Most Sweet Jesus » ni la version française.

rows.title: Sacred Heart Aspiration
rows.sourceAnchor: Sacred Heart of Jesus, I place all my trust in you
rows.appAnchor: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, I place all my trust in you
rows.sourceScope: Indexed USCCB Sacred Heart novena references an aspiration 'Sacred Heart of Jesus, I place all my trust in you'; app begins 'Most Sacred Heart of Jesus'. Source is the 2026 Novena article (2024 Dilexit Nos and Leo XIV references) rather than original historical prayer edition; direct page fetch returned 403. Never infer primary Latin/French sources from novena prose.

readerDisclosure.en: The indexed USCCB Sacred Heart novena mentions “Sacred Heart of Jesus, I place all my trust in you”; the card adds “Most”. This modern novena article is a contextual comparator, not the original short aspiration or evidence for its Latin and French forms.
readerDisclosure.fr: La neuvaine du Sacré-Cœur indexée par l’USCCB cite « Sacred Heart of Jesus, I place all my trust in you » ; la carte ajoute « Most ». Cet article récent sert de comparaison, non d’édition originale de la courte invocation ni de preuve des versions latine et française.

rows.title: De Profundis — Psalm 129
rows.sourceAnchor: O UT of the depths I have cried to Thee
rows.appAnchor: Out of the depths I have cried to thee
rows.sourceScope: With God/Evening Prayers includes Psalm 129 plus further versicle/response and collect. App renders the psalm with selected Eternal Rest and May they rest in peace lines, omitting historic O Lord hear my prayer and collect. It is a devotional excerpt/assembly not solely TYPOGRAPHY_NORMALIZED. Historic Clement XII/Pius VI indulgence discussion not current grant.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited prayer book follows Psalm 129 with further versicles and a collect that this card does not reproduce. The card combines the psalm with a shorter prayer for the dead; it is an adapted devotional assembly, not just typography. Old indulgence remarks are historical.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le livre cité fait suivre le psaume 129 d’autres versets et d’une oraison absents de cette carte. Celle-ci unit le psaume à une prière abrégée pour les défunts ; c’est un assemblage dévotionnel, non une simple adaptation typographique. Les indulgences anciennes sont historiques.

rows.title: Litany of Saint Joseph
rows.sourceScope: The USCCB expressly says its English translation incorporating seven 2021 invocations and specified alternate intro/conclusion was adapted and approved by Committee on Divine Worship. App English includes invocation set. This does not make the French translation conference-approved or establish independent printed 1909 litany collation; separate historically earlier and current forms.

readerDisclosure.en: This is the expanded Saint Joseph litany with seven invocations added in 2021. The USCCB approves its published English translation, not automatically this app’s French or Latin wording; it is not the unexpanded 1909 edition.
readerDisclosure.fr: Il s’agit des litanies de saint Joseph augmentées de sept invocations en 2021. L’USCCB approuve sa traduction anglaise publiée, sans certifier d’office les textes français ou latin de l’application ; ce n’est pas la forme de 1909 non augmentée.

rows.title: To Thee, O Blessed Joseph
rows.sourceScope: Official English Quamquam pluries page appends a Prayer to Saint Joseph with the inherited app English incipit and full structural sequence; some spelling/typography differs (off-spring vs offspring). Latin encyclical page says the prayer was circulated with the letter, but does not print its Latin body on that page; it cannot prove this app's complete Latin and French texts.

readerDisclosure.en: Leo XIII’s English encyclical page includes this Saint Joseph prayer as an appendix; the Latin encyclical page refers to the attached prayer but does not print its text there. The Latin and French versions require separate witness collation.
readerDisclosure.fr: La page anglaise de l’encyclique de Léon XIII comprend cette prière à saint Joseph en annexe ; la page latine renvoie à la prière jointe sans en reproduire le texte. Les versions latine et française exigent des témoins à collationner séparément.

rows.title: Veni Sancte Spiritus · Pentecost Sequence
rows.sourceScope: Historical Raccolta explicitly contains the Veni Sancte Spiritus Latin sequence and the English Caswall hymn with the app's exact English opening; English lines and punctuation vary editorially; transcription also has OCR artifacts in Latin. The historical indulgence grants on that page must not be presented as current or presently applicable. No independent full printed or French translation collation.

readerDisclosure.en: The 1857 Raccolta witnesses the English Pentecost sequence beginning “Holy Spirit! Lord of light!”. Its historical indulgence provisions are not evidence of a current grant. The scanned edition and French translation still require independent collation.
readerDisclosure.fr: La Raccolta de 1857 atteste la séquence anglaise commençant par « Holy Spirit! Lord of light! ». Les indulgences historiques de cette page ne constituent pas une concession actuelle. La collation de l’imprimé et du français reste à effectuer.

rows.title: Prayer for All the Faithful Departed
rows.sourceAnchor: give to the souls of thy servants departed
rows.appAnchor: grant to the souls of thy servants departed
rows.sourceScope: Historical Catholic Prayer Book transcribes 'give to the souls' and fuller Trinitarian conclusion 'with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost'. The app English has 'grant to the souls' and shorter conclusion. It is a distinct English rendering, not verbatim from that 19th-century witness; Latin and French remain uncollated.

readerDisclosure.en: The cited historical Prayer Book prints “give to the souls” and a longer Trinitarian conclusion. The app says “grant to the souls” and uses a shorter ending. These are distinct English witnesses, not an exact reproduction of the cited edition.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le livre ancien cité donne « give to the souls » et une conclusion trinitaire plus longue. L’application emploie « grant to the souls » et une finale abrégée. Il s’agit de textes anglais distincts, non d’une reproduction exacte de l’édition citée.

rows.title: Eternal Rest · for one deceased person
rows.appAnchor: Eternal rest grant unto him or her
rows.sourceScope: Catholic Truth Society prints the singular formula with alternatives 'him (her)' and response indicators. App expands as 'him or her' and omits the dialogical rubric; should not be called verbatim exact CTS English. French singular neutral phrasing and Latin separate source not certified.

readerDisclosure.en: The Catholic Truth Society gives alternatives “him (her)” with response markings. This card expands them to “him or her” and omits the response cues. Its English is an accessible devotional rendering, not an exact transcription of that page.
readerDisclosure.fr: La Catholic Truth Society imprime « him (her) » avec les marques de réponse. Cette carte développe en « him or her » et omet les indications dialoguées. C’est une formulation dévotionnelle pratique, non une transcription exacte de cette page.

rows.title: Sub Tuum Praesidium
rows.sourceScope: The 29 September 2018 Holy See communiqué prints Sub tuum in Latin plus a brief English version 'We fly to Thy protection'; the app preserves the traditional English 'We fly to your patronage'. This is not identical English text, and is no complete French/Latin print comparison.

readerDisclosure.en: The Holy See communiqué prints the Latin Sub tuum with an English rendering beginning “We fly to Thy protection”. The app preserves the traditional “We fly to your patronage”. These are not verbatim English twins; the French witness is uncollated.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le communiqué romain donne le latin et une traduction anglaise débutant par « We fly to Thy protection ». L’application conserve « We fly to your patronage ». Ces versions anglaises ne sont pas identiques ; la source française reste à collationner.

rows.title: Adoremus in aeternum · Psalm 116/117
rows.appAnchor: Let us adore for ever the Most Holy Sacrament
rows.sourceScope: Blessed Sacrament Book landing/title page prints Adoremus antiphon but does not publish the complete app sequence Psalm 116/117 plus Gloria there. St Gregory Hymnal Project Gutenberg HTML supplies the complete Latin refrain, psalm, and Gloria sequence as a secondary 1910s historical comparator; source edition and English/French exact translations still not fully collated.

readerDisclosure.en: The 1913 Blessed Sacrament Book page attests the “Adoremus in aeternum” antiphon, but not this complete Psalm 116 and doxology arrangement. The historical St Gregory Hymnal is a separate comparator for that sequence, not a certified facsimile of this app’s English and French.
readerDisclosure.fr: La page du Blessed Sacrament Book de 1913 atteste l’antienne « Adoremus in aeternum », mais non l’ensemble du psaume 116 et de la doxologie de cette carte. Le St Gregory Hymnal sert de témoin distinct pour cet ordre, non de fac-similé certifié des traductions anglaise et française.

supportingWitness.en: St Gregory Hymnal · antiphon, Psalm 116 and doxology
supportingWitness.fr: St Gregory Hymnal · antienne, psaume 116 et doxologie

rows.title: Litany of Loreto · 1962-era form
rows.sourceScope: The original inventory's Vatican Loreto URL is a current expanded form with Mother of Mercy, Mother of Hope and Solace of Migrants, none of which belongs to the 1962-era invocation set. The reader already overrides the main link to a qualified older comparison. Keep the 2020 source as contrast, never 1962 printed proof.

readerDisclosure.en: The original catalogue's Vatican link gives the expanded Litany with later invocations, not the 1962-era text. The reader links an older comparative prayer-book witness instead; neither link is a certified 1962 printed facsimile.
readerDisclosure.fr: Le lien du catalogue d’origine mène aux Litanies augmentées par des invocations ultérieures, et non au texte de l’époque de 1962. Le lecteur renvoie plutôt à un livre ancien comparatif ; aucun de ces liens ne certifie un imprimé de 1962.

rows.title: Litany of Loreto · current invocations
rows.sourceScope: The linked Vatican Loreto page currently includes Mother of Mercy, Mother of Hope and Solace of Migrants. Their existence supports the distinction from the older form but does not independently collate all 3 languages and invocation punctuation.

readerDisclosure.en: The linked Holy See Litany contains later invocations, consistent with the present expanded form. This source comparison is not a complete English, French and Latin transcription certificate.
readerDisclosure.fr: Les Litanies publiées par le Saint-Siège comportent des invocations ajoutées ultérieurement, conformément à la forme augmentée. Cette comparaison ne certifie pas l’intégralité des trois versions linguistiques.
